This is the first time I've tried a game of this type, a free-to-play game, and I didn't really enjoy it. It's just not my genre. I usually only play single-player games, but it was recommended to me, so I decided to give it a try and see what it was like.

I played a bit of the campaign and spent some time in the open world as well, including completing a dungeon. Visually, the game looks great, and I didn't experience any performance issues.

From a narrative standpoint, I found the beginning of the campaign pretty weak. It doesn't really hook you or make you want to keep playing, and it's also difficult to understand what's going on in the story. I'm not sure if that improves later on.

The open world was decent and about what you'd expect. There were animals, enemies, side quests, and so on. My main issue with this game—and I think I'd probably feel the same way about other games in this genre—is that it throws way too much information at you. You're constantly getting new items, abilities, rewards, and many other things. I found it overwhelming and somewhat confusing because there were a lot of mechanics I didn't fully understand.

The combat seemed good from what I played, although it looks like it's quite deep and offers a lot of different combinations and build options.

I wouldn't recommend this game to someone like me who mainly plays single-player games, but if you're curious about it, I encourage you to give it a try. It's free, after all.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that cosmetics and in-game clothing options are predominantly locked behind cash purchases or require spending real money.

citations.review_text:
Game is fine, graphics are nice. 

But the monetization here makes other gacha games look like saints by comparison. 30,000+ USD boats, outfits that cost more than even the most expensive ultra premium deluxe versions of the most anticipated games...

That payment model may work for people who have thousands of dollars worth of disposable income, but if you want to look good and you don't have that kind of money to throw around, I hope you're ready to grind for hours just to get a mediocre looking outfit. I think the game is really solid and the gameplay is actually not the reason why I don't recommend it. Not that the cosmetics you get are bad cause you do get some just that they were made inferior to paid options on purpose to make you spend money on cosmetics, but if you don't care about clothing and things like that then, YES I do recommend it.

The premise of the game is great and I get that it wants to be a live service game similar to MMO's but still let you play solo. But it is way too overwhelming. I played the game for several hours now and dont even know how far I am or if I am even doing it correct. It is also filled with in-game purchases. I get that its mostly just cosmetics, but the game throws those at you like its necessary to participate in that. I cant recommend this game because I dont understand 95% of it.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game world and progression systems feature excessive menus and convoluted nested interfaces.

citations.review_text:
I saw a couple of shorts on youtube, advertising the game and asked the viewers about some of my curiosities regarding it, however i never got a reply… hence i decided to go full on Thanos mode (fine… i’ll do it myself) and thus… here we are.

The game has some very good graphics. The visuals are indeed awesome.
The combat seems quite interesting.
The game gives you a lot of content. It will keep you occupied.
YOU CAN PET ANIMALS!

But now we move to the problems of a casual player’s point of view.

The game is ridiculously convoluted. God help us, everything I did would activate a new system that had systems in its systems with systems and menus in the menu of a menu that was made of menus. Later I was trying to find the same functions and I could not in the mess of so many menus.
I also have a bone to pick with how fake the freedom of picking different fighting styles appeared in this gacha game.
Also very poorly made is the way you experience the story, cause you are not allowed to progress with the story if you don’t play other aspects of the game.
Bad explanations. From prompting you on self healing before that is possible, to telling you that healers are gonna heal you for free for also being a healer (fake)... we have many functions that are not explained correctly. I tried the animal moves training and while it looked like I was doing nothing wrong, the game was failing me constantly. Turns out the instructions were wrong.
You find some special insects that you need to grab and the game tells you, shoot them down… I did… nothing happened. I ran towards them, grabbed it as it was flying around, victory.
You unlock a skill to grab things from a distance, game tells you you can disarm enemies with it and to go practice on some bandits... it does not activate… I tried several times and only days later I found out how to use the snatch skill. Not to mention that the first time I passed by a snake camp I was prompted to use that skill to grab the ite…

Game is a little too Chinese for me. 

Not that I don't like Chinese games, I do, I am just obviously not the target audience here. The systems are quite overwhelming, there's a large focus on cosmetics, there's a lot of currencies, gacha, and everything is just like an absolute fire hose of information. All the information is *there* for you to figure it out, but it doesn't do a lot of leg work trying to introduce the player to these systems in a way that you can comfortably orient yourself with them. 

I do think the character creation is interesting, and the trailers looked like there were some fun systems but I found myself so overwhelmed with information 3 hours into the game, that I asked myself "will I be getting back on this tomorrow?" and I sadly answered no. Meaning I never really got to engage with some of the things I saw in the trailers, because with how everything else went, I was afraid it would take me forever and I would have to slog through more whirlwind quests with 1 million rewards and fight against the controls even more. Simply not worth it for me. 

So, I don't know. Maybe I'm just too American for this game and prefer a different style of game to this. You might enjoy it if you're into the Chinese style of games like this-- it reminded me a lot of Dyson-sphere program in a lot of ways lol.

Although i do recommend the game, as it has the bones and atmosphere of something special, it is bogged down by ALOT of unnesseary bloat that does nothing to enrich the experience, only over complicate it. The good thing is, to an extent you can ignore most of what you dont like, including most of the insane menu system and just focus on exploring the world. The combat is fun, the upgrade and character progression system once again have the basis of something good, but most of that is buried underneath convoluted systems and subsystems and even sub systems of subsystems. The world is gorgeous and fun to explore. If you treat this game like your next main game or something youll probably get flustered at how overly complicated everything is. But if you go into it like i did, with the mindset of just checking it out, casually enjoying the parts that appeal to me, then i think this game has a lot of fun to offer, for free which is just as insane as the menu system here.

I would like to recommend this as it does look like fun, but the execution of attracting new players is absolutely horrible. 

I don't have an issue with in medias res in general, but here it is just done so poorly. You lose your magic macguffin and presumably want to get it back but no explanation as to why you should care. You are thrown into a massive but soulless open-world with neither the interest in getting your thing back or exploration because why would you bother doing a lot of side missions with no idea why you should care about your character.

Another big issue is the menus on-top of menus on-top of tabs with some sub-menus on the side. At least try to ease people into this bloated UI hellscape by maybe weaving them into the narrative introducing them with a bit of breathing room in-between. It just feels like the game was focused on creating a lot of content and then just drop it en masse, not caring about tying it together.

The game is very fun on Expert Mode, especially if you have experience with Soulslike games

Parry system is quite forgiving, quests + story are fun
And the combat in general is very fluid even with a controller.

Does this game have too many menus? Yes. But don't think too much of it. Lots of community resources to guide you through the maze and focus on the essentials. Even within the game players leave notes that help you with exploration etc. :) Given that this game is truly free to play, it is very worth giving it a shot. Focus mainly on story to level up faster.

The premise of the game is great and I get that it wants to be a live service game similar to MMO's but still let you play solo. But it is way too overwhelming. There are like a thousand different menus and I am literally confused as to what they do and what am I to do in each of them. Maybe I am stupid, but holy hell. I played the game for several hours now and dont even know how far I am or if I am even doing it correct. It is also filled with in-game purchases. I get that its mostly just cosmetics, but the game throws those at you like its necessary to participate in that. I cant recommend this game because I dont understand 95% of it.

citations.review_text:
I don't know how is this game free?!

This game is massive and packed with so much stuff to do that it can provide you with hundreds of hours of entertainment for free. You are never really forced to spend any money. And the things you can buy with real money are just skins and such which are completely optional. 

Want to play this game as a mmorpg? You can there is a multiplayer mode. 
Want to play it coop with friends? You can do that as well
Want to play it solo as an action adventure game? Yes you can do it, I think that is the main way to play the game.

There are so many things to do in the game.
Want to build your base like in sims? You can
Want to roam the beautiful world with great graphics pet cats and dogs, heal ducks and other goofy stuff? You can
Want to fight mobs in the open world as well as world bosses? You can
Want to play pvp in arena in 1v1 or 3v3? You can
Want to play pve with other people against a boss? You can
Want to play a battle royale style game mode? You can

I am like 60 hours in and am close to finishing exploration of the first main area and I think I have explored only like 20% of the world and interracted with like 30% of mechanics.

The main complaint from people is the very complicated menu sistem which I agree with. Menus upon menus upon menus, but with so much stuff in the game can you blame them? I honestly have no idea what would be a better aproach to pack all of the stuff and not be overwhelmed by the menus. After 60 hours I still have a hard time sometimes finding the menu that I am looking for. 

Other complaints are that the game is not polished, and sure with so much content some is bound to be a mess, but since the game is free and does not force you to spend any money I feel like I have no right to expect everything to be perfect. 

There is a gambling system in the shop and for some stuff that you need to upgrade your skills. Like for example to obtain some scrolls to upgrade one part of your skills you need to open …

Such a fun open-world game, there's so much to do and explore. The UI and menus can be a bit confusing when you first start out but once you get used to it it's very straightforward. 
There's a gacha element but it honestly is optional, there's a lot of different ways to level up your character without spending anything or doing hours of grinding. 
The online community is great and helpful, but solo mode has a lot to offer as well so that you don't feel like you're missing out. 
The graphics are great and the game runs smoothly for me but if you have a lower spec pc you might have to fiddle with the settings or only play in solo mode.
I really recommend this game to anyone who wants a game where you can both fight and explore to your heart's content. I'm honestly having a blast playing it and discovering everything there is to see and do.

Game- 10/10
Menus- Too many/10

At first this seemed like a pretty solid game with ARPG elements baked into it, and plenty of things to explore and discover. However, you'll hit a huge brick wall for progression due to the time-gating of currencies and other resources, like daily Energy and Stamina amounts. Once you're in the endgame for farming, you'll only play for a few minutes every few days due to these constraints once they replenish a bit.


The Inner Ways (big damage abilities) will require a significant amount of specific "currencies" but are mostly acquired through gacha mechanics, so if you're unlucky, you're going to take forever to actually gain any real progress in that department.


Also, the overwhelming amount of menus and submenus buried within the (arguably) intentionally confusing UI is just a complete mess. I don't know how many hours it took me to actually get a feel for the menus, because half the time I was navigating through them, I'd forget what the hell I was doing or looking for in the first place.


If you want a game where your time is actually valued and you can make meaningful progression, play ANYTHING else.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as heavily reliant on precise timing for parries.

citations.review_text:
The game’s combat system is 90% about parrying, and you have to time it within a 0.0001-second window at least 20–30 times in a row during a single fight.

The combat animations are deliberately designed so that there are at least ten different versions of a ten-frame animation, with each version differing by only a single frame. As a result, you basically have to guess when to block or parry.

There are also attack animations that can kill you on the very first frame, meaning you have to block or parry before the attack even begins.

That is not difficult—it is simply pointless frustration deliberately created for the people playing the game.

[h1] Poor Experience[/h1]

The game has AA graphics and weight, but it functions like a mobile game, with gacha elements and level progression limits; character advancement depends on luck or excessive repetition.

A very beautiful world and quality setting, but the open world itself is quite generic, with repetitive missions, superficial dialogues, and shallow NPCs. The visuals and animations are the only "memorable" things at times (the voice acting is simply awful). The use of AI for dialogues increases this feeling of artificiality instead of enriching the narrative.

The combat system, which seems to be the game's high point, is unbalanced and unresponsive. The enemies are sponges with no strategy whatsoever, and the bosses are even worse; you deal almost no damage. Parrying is the only viable thing for combat to work, and even then, the fights are quite frustrating regardless of your character's level or equipment.

The game is disappointing, unfortunately.

It was fun for a while but the world feels really kinda barren. And the description doesn't make it apparent that it's actually a MMO. I think your settings can exclude you from seeing other people but you'll see the millions of 'signposts' they drop everywhere, can be a little immersion breaking.

The story is... interesting, if a bit hard to follow, and the combat feels nice but is a bit, shall we say, overtuned. Even if you have the parry assist setting on, some bosses are really quite ridiculous. I think your character also gets put into a kind of 'recovery' state when you miss a parry, preventing you from parrying any follow-up attacks, which can then extend that time, meaning if you miss the first parry in a hit combo then you're eating the entire combo.

You can also block and dodge, which are separate actions from (attempting a) parry, but as far as I could tell there was zero reason to block - because then you miss the opportunity to parry, and still take damage, so you might as well have dodged - though dodging is quite necessary to avoid 'red attacks' that can't be parried.

But at the end of the day, it's free, so you lose nothing but your time by trying it out.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the English localization and voice acting rely heavily on artificial intelligence, resulting in poor quality and unnatural sounding dialogue.

citations.review_text:
The amount of stuff you can do in this game is insane. Huge free roaming, tons of side quests, fishing lol, pvp, pve, solo, guilds, events. Online co-op, and more.    The first thing that I noticed is the amount of depth in the questing. The main story, boss quests, and the "lost chapters" the amount of intense emotion, lore and great cut scenes are insane for a free to play game. Im only 40 hours in but Ive had quests tug at my heart strings, made me hold my breath or just say "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥."      There are a ton of menus in this game and it can feel overwhelming when first starting out, So i recommend reading the screen prompts when they show up or watching a youtube video to understand them better. Gameplay is a little wonky starting out but literally after about an hour I didnt even notice it anymore. Elite character customization, i dont remember the exact amount of different weapons to play with but I think its roughly around 10 or so. And each weapon can be paired with unique passives and buffs to fit your style. Some aspects are a bit grindy later but honestly there is so much to do I dont even notice.  

Overall: This game is a solid 8 maybe 9/10  Rating for a free to play game? 12/10
Its free so you can always uninstall it if you dont vibe with it. 

*It does have AI translation for the languages so it can get confusing at times, thats my only nitpick but it is also free to play so it cancels it out LOL

I stumbled on this game browsing the trending section and saw that it was free. This game is absolute peak for a free game. It's open world and you can wander about at your own pace; the environment is expansive & quite scenic. From my first few hours, there's plenty of sidequests to derail you from the main storyline. 

There's obviously some flaws like sometimes its glitchy like with a half-open door in the ruined temple (one with the roided-out white horse boss) which makes you climb for some reason?

I spent a good bit of time just screwing around with the AI character customization.
Lets you pet cats but not dogs, boo.

I can attest that this game is relatively well optimized, my aging blower RX Vega 56 held up at 60 FPS more or less at Performance & Balanced settings. Although during the change to phase 3 for the 黑財神 (God of Avarice) boss, it overheated my GPU; but that's probably due to age and its poor blower design.

I personally haven't played with the English audio (playing w/ CN audio + ENG sub), but from watching videos of others playing, it sounds absolutely terrible and needs better work; not relying so heavily on AI. 紅缐 (Ruby)'s ENG voice is of a grown woman's.

For a free MMORPG, I didn't really expect much. However, It's safe to say I was pretty surprised! The game has beautiful graphics, story, and so much to do. I was pretty overwhelmed at first, but I'm about a hundred hours in the game and I still haven't done everything. Plenty of exploration is encouraged, engaging side stories you can play through, and a good blend of MMORPG and ARPG play styles. 
The only complaint I have is the poor use of AI translation and localization for the global version. Characters begin to sound funny and the same due to repetitive use of the same AI voices later on in the game. The translation also tends to make no sense. Many areas lag at times where there is noticeable clipping. While this does throw off my experience from time to time, it's not absolutely unbearable.
Overall, I highly recommend if you're a fan of open world experiences!

P.S: Pet all the kitties!! :)

claims.claim: The game features demanding storage requirements, occupying around 160GB to 200GB of disk space.

citations.review_text:
I really like this game, so why am I not playing it?
The answer: Almost 200GB for something that could be 80GB and fast to install.

Like many others, I felt the menus were just way too bloated. Even after 600+ hours, I still think there's a lot of unnecessary systems that only make the game more confusing. It feels redundant rather than adding depth.

I also got tired of constantly upgrading equipment every breakthrough, along with the time gated progression that feels like a mobile game, which is something I dislike the most. The game started off amazing, but with almost every update, it slowly went downhill for me.

That said, I did spend months playing with a guild, and those were genuinely some of the best moments I had. The social experience made the game much more enjoyable, so credit where credit is due.

What I loved most were the boss fights, the beautiful visuals, and the main story in Kaifeng. The Lianzhou region was another highlight. The snowy landscape offered a refreshing change of scenery. On the other hand, many side quests dragged on with excessive, unskippable dialogue, making them feel more like a chore than enjoyable content.

My biggest issue with the world itself is how empty some areas feel, especially Hexi. It's such a massive region, yet so much of it feels barren, lifeless, and unfinished.

Where BUGS Meet. It's honestly crazy that this game now takes up around 170GB of storage and has earned millions from players, yet there still doesn't seem to be any urgency in fixing long standing bugs. That's pretty ridiculous.

At its peak, this game was easily a 9/10 experience for me. I genuinely had an amazing time. But after more than 700 hours as i also played on the other client, I'd rate it around 6.5/10 at most.

Would I recommend it? Yes, because it's free. For a free game, there's a lot to enjoy, especially the combat, visuals, and some of the story content. Just be prepared for the flaws to become more noticeable the longer you play. Eventually, the repetitive systems, bugs, and frustrating design choices start to pile up, and they can really wear you down.
Great Game. Lots of downloads and storage space though.

TLDR ; lazy quest design and takes up too much space.

160 GB is not justified at all. Other games look better, have more system, and have better quests/minigames than this. Online play is garbage and the solo mode is fun until you get to Hexi, then it becomes a pixel hunt.

Review written after 1,600 hours of gameplay and having experienced a wide range of situations in the game:

- Several bugs: broken world map textures, glitched interactions, bugged building items...

- Reports and bug reports are ignored: Bugs remain unresolved no matter how many times they are reported, and players reported for violations listed in the report options—including spam, inappropriate audio, cheating, and other disruptive behavior—are never punished.

- Extremely expensive cash shop: Want to look fancy? You have to pay real money to get Pearls. There is absolutely no way to earn premium currency for free (not even a small monthly allowance for F2P players).

- Instead of fixing these structural issues, every new patch just adds more cosmetics to the cash shop and shallow, cash-driven events.

- Terrible PvP system: Horrible balance that forces the player base to use the exact same rigid META builds and weapons.

- Insane lag and terrible optimization.

- Confusing UI: Cluttered menus that lack any proper explanation.

- Boring story quests: Long, tedious conversations and forced slow-walking segments that completely kill the pacing.

- Lack of content variety: Repetitive NPC models and a complete lack of voice acting.

- A Toxic Community: Because it is a free MMORPG, it attracts many toxic, weird, creepy, and attention-seeking players. The community is one of the strangest and most toxic in the MMO genre. Many guilds have an unhealthy, cult-like mindset where defending the game’s flaws matters more than criticism. Leaving a guild feels like being erased — friendships often end instantly. The game revolves around social status, creating endless drama and ego clashes.

- Global chat is constantly flooded with spam: Players beg continuously for shop outfits, Pearls, gallery exhibition votes, and sect rank votes, often repeating the same requests through unsolicited DMs. This creates an endless 24/7 scroll that makes the chat channels annoying, intrusive,…

Worst netcode ive ever seen and its funny cause this game makes Tekken netcode feel pristine. Want to see players in pvp teleport while you have 26ms ? Knock yourself out. 

Storywise - you wont understand much except that you are maybe a prodigy and fight your way through the events of your life, although it feels like each chapter is a dream (especially the bosses). Captivating ? Not even close. Typical Chinese bs story.

Minigames - all of them are chinese minigames or dumbed down versions for us, europeans and americans i guess. Overall, more chinese bs from which you understand nothing. 

Gameplay - parry system is better than .... ghost of tsushima and for a console reference, ghost of yotei. This game cannot hold a candle to the parry system in titles like Sekiro. Spam parry and you win or you lose. 50/50 chance. Attacks feel somewhat slow and slugish but in PVP, the only thing that matters is if you pay for geforce now to lower your ms to under 10 and have the advantage of .......... faster animations. Yes ladies and gents, faster animations = you can parry attacks from your opponent while they cannot if their ms is over 20 :) Enjoy suffering. 

Game is an absolute joke where at least 40% of the playerbase have paid absurd prices for outfits and skins and animation skins. Given the fact that its also available on android (phone) - no wonder its a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cash grab. 

Good things about the game:
Graphics (and not everytime cause you can find plenty of textures that are resembling those from PS2 era) 
........

Thats it. Really. 

I have over 800 hours in the game and have been drip fed like the others to the point where i started losing interest and frankly, if you want to play the game, go for it. Play till the last expansion, dont get fooled into buying ANYTHING from their cash shop unless you are a rich spoiled brat with access to mommy and daddy's bank accounts.

Want a comparison or to see how their other games ended up - look no furthe…

I don't think this game is awful, in fact, i think it's a good game that is worthy of a try. But it's also a game where I would hesitate to truly recommend. 

It's a game with an incredible presentation and commitment to its theme. From world design to costume design, done in an extremely masterful and tasteful way. There are some immersion breaking mechanic like the BOTW tears of the kingdom vehicle crafting system, but it's entirely optional and can be totally ignored.

Yet at the same time this game want to be your one and only game due to its long list of things that it want you to do on the daily basis, while does not provide the sufficient amount of content nor variety to justify the amount of commitment you need to make to ensure you are kept up in the endgame. 

The boss fights, while fun for the first time, hell, maybe even the tenth times (mostly carried by the crazy shenanigans that can happen in coop), will stop being so fun on the twentieth. The fight design is also not exactly deep, and often come down to some very simple mechanic that is communicated to the player in a very insufficient way which can cause a lot of trial and error. A mechanic that, when failed, is often result in a full wipe  with little counter play allowed. It's similar to FFXIV in term of fight design. But unlike FFXIV where the fight is fully scripted down to the minute, and a successful clear look like a beautiful and elaborate dance off between the boss and the players, in WWM, it's more of a free style where the both party just hoping for the best. That is to say, the mechanics are clunky and sometimes bug ridden, or so poorly designed that they can overlap which randomly caused an unavoidable wipe.

I also got tired of constantly upgrading equipment every breakthrough, along with the time gated progression that feels like a mobile game, which is something I dislike the most. The game started off amazing, but with almost every update, it slowly went downhill for me.

That said, I did spend months playing with a guild, and those were genuinely some of the best moments I had. The social experience made the game much more enjoyable, so credit where credit is due.

On the other hand, many side quests dragged on with excessive, unskippable dialogue, making them feel more like a chore than enjoyable content.

My biggest issue with the world itself is how empty some areas feel, especially Hexi. It's such a massive region, yet so much of it feels barren, lifeless, and unfinished.

Just be prepared for the flaws to become more noticeable the longer you play. Eventually, the repetitive systems, bugs, and frustrating design choices start to pile up, and they can really wear you down.

Overall: Beautiful, and incredibly customizable — but ultimately too casual for what I was looking for.

Where Winds Meet is a gorgeous game with a lot going for it. The world is beautiful, the character customization is fantastic, and there’s a lot of attention to detail that makes the game enjoyable to explore. Honestly, the visuals and customization alone kept me interested for longer than I probably would have otherwise.

However, as someone who leans toward the semi-hardcore side of gaming, the actual gameplay and progression didn't quite scratch the itch for me.

The biggest issue is that the game doesn't demand much time, investment, or skill. Most of the PvE content feels relatively easy, and there isn't much that feels genuinely challenging or mechanically demanding. I still regularly see PUGs struggling with some PvE content, but at the same time, the difficulty itself doesn't feel particularly rewarding. The addition of AI companions also makes it possible to clear content without necessarily relying on other players, which I assume is intended to make the game more accessible.

If you're looking for content that actually tests your mechanical skill, PvP is probably where the game shines the most. Outside of that, I found myself wishing there were more difficult PvE encounters, deeper optimization, and more meaningful reasons to push my character further.

The gacha is also far too expensive for what it offers. For a game that is otherwise so generous with customization, the monetization can feel particularly excessive.

Ultimately, I think Where Winds Meet is a great game for casual players. You don't need to sink huge amounts of time into it, you can progress at your own pace, and there's plenty to explore and customize. But for players who enjoy min-maxing, difficult PvE, optimization, progression, and constantly having something challenging to work toward, I don't think there's quite enough here.
